title: Confession and Inheritance
premise: Retired detective Dominic Sandoval, drowning in debt at his failing bookshop, is hired by a nervous woman named Vera to prove that her brother Aldous will be murdered — a crime that hasn't happened yet but that she insists is already written into the family's shipping business. When Aldous turns up dead exactly as predicted, Dominic realizes the killer is following a coded ledger hidden in the shop's own inventory, a ledger his late partner left behind and one that implicates Dominic's own survival bargain from decades ago. As the statute of limitations on an old cover-up expires, Dominic must choose between protecting the people who once saved him and exposing a confession that will destroy them all; in the end he publishes the truth, loses the shop, and gains something rarer — an unburdened conscience.
about_author: Rosalind Ravensworth spent fifteen years cataloguing rare books in a coastal auction house before turning to crime fiction full-time. She writes in the margins of ledgers she refuses to explain.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Dominic Sandoval's POV. A woman named Vera Ilyich pays triple rate for Dominic to prevent a murder that hasn't happened yet — her brother's, dated three weeks out. The emotional beat: wary curiosity masking financial desperation as Dominic pockets money he knows he shouldn't.

chapters.title: The Inventory Nobody Reads
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Cataloguing stock for a loan audit, he finds anomalies: certain books shelved by date rather than author, spines marked with pinpricks. Emotional beat: unease — the pattern feels familiar, like handwriting he once knew.

chapters.title: Aldous Ilyich, Alive and Loud
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He interviews the supposed future victim, a charming shipping magnate who laughs off the threat and offers Dominic a retainer to drop Vera's case. Beat: temptation and suspicion — why does a man about to die seem so rehearsed?

chapters.title: What My Partner Left Me
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with flashback. The ledger's cipher matches the shorthand of Marcus Hale, Dominic's late partner, whose death twenty years ago was ruled accidental. Beat: grief resurfacing, guilt tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: Vera's Version
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. She reveals the family firm launders money through book shipments, and that Aldous planned to confess everything on a deadline — making his death convenient for everyone. Beat: fear braided with resentment toward a brother she both loves and blames.

chapters.title: The First Entry
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Deciphering the first ledger entry, he finds a payment dated the week Marcus died — signed with initials that could be his own. Beat: cold dread; the past is not what he remembers.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His old contact, prosecutor Nadia Okafor, warns him the statute on the original cover-up expires in nineteen days — after which the truth becomes legally worthless. Beat: urgency reframing everything; time itself is now the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Shop Gets a Visitor
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A polite stranger buys every copy of one obscure title, then warns Dominic that some inventories are better left uncounted. Beat: menace wrapped in courtesy; the stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Sisters and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera admits she hired Dominic not to save Aldous but to expose him — she wants the confession forced into daylight before the statute kills it. Beat: betrayal curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Marcus's Last Case File
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In a storage unit, he finds Marcus's notes: evidence that young Detective Sandoval took a bribe to bury a death connected to the Ilyich firm — the price of saving his dying sister. Beat: shame; the theme of survival's price lands on the protagonist himself.

chapters.title: The Deadline Moves Up
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aldous announces an early public confession, and the ledger's next entry re-dates the murder to forty-eight hours ahead. Beat: panic; the prediction is updating in real time, meaning the killer is watching them watch it.

chapters.title: Nadia's Bargain
chapters.summary: Nadia Okafor's POV. She offers Dominic immunity for testimony that would implicate him alongside the Ilyichs. Beat: moral vertigo — justice offered as a trap.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating Dominic and Vera POVs. They stake out Aldous's estate; a staged break-in nearly kills Vera, and Dominic realizes the 'prediction' was designed to lure witnesses. Beat: terror and protectiveness; loyalty tested under fire.

chapters.title: The Empty Confession
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aldous vanishes hours before his confession, leaving a typed statement that names no names. Beat: despair — the truth slipping through their fingers like sand.

chapters.title: Decoding the Whole Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, all-night sequence. Working from Marcus's shorthand, he reconstructs the full ledger: decades of payments, and a final entry in fresh ink naming the person who inherited the operation when Marcus died. Beat: grim clarity; the cipher was never hidden, just unread.

chapters.title: The Inheritor
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. The final entry points to the family's quiet accountant — and to Vera herself as designated successor, a role she never knew she'd been groomed for. Beat: horror of inheritance; identity upended.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Confronting the accountant at the docks, Dominic learns Marcus wasn't murdered by the firm — he died forcing the ledger into existence, and the accountant has been waiting for someone to finish reading it. Beat: tragic revelation; grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What Aldous Knew
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aldous is found alive, held by parties who wanted his confession buried; his testimony completes the chain from old bribe to present murder plot. Beat: catharsis deferred — the last piece clicking home.

chapters.title: The Statute Expires
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At midnight on the deadline, Dominic chooses truth over protection: he files everything, including his own crime. Beat: sacrifice; the price of survival finally paid in full.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the stand, he confesses to the twenty-year-old cover-up while dismantling the conspiracy around the Ilyich firm. Beat: exposure as liberation; the courtroom silent around his voice.

chapters.title: Closing the Shop
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera, cleared but changed, helps Dominic box the last inventory; the shop is sold to pay his legal debts. Beat: bittersweet loss — the ledger's pages finally blank.

chapters.title: An Unburdened Conscience
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue. Months later, working as a records clerk, Dominic receives a postcard from Vera and a note from Nadia: the first conviction landed. He starts writing his own account — in plain language this time. Beat: quiet peace earned, not given.
